::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[3 unknown, 3 nonlinear equations of form $xy - z =$ constant](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1385877/3-unknown-3-nonlinear-equations-of-form-xy-z-constant), asked by [doc holiday](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/259157/doc-holiday) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-08-05; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> How can I solve:     $$xy - z = a$$
>                       $$xz - y = b$$
>                      $$yz - x = c$$ 
>          for $x, y, z$ (where $a,b,c$ are constants)?   Let all variables and constants be integers 
>          (or at least rational)
:::

The brute force method would be to isolate (“solve for”) $z$ in the third equation (assuming $y \neq 0$), and substitute into the first two.  That gives two nonlinear equations in two variables $x$ and $y$.  Then repeat: isolate either $y$ or $x$ in one of those new equations, and substitute into the other.  That should result in one (probably nonlinear) equation for one of the variables.
